discussion_comments.comment_body: `prepareHandoffRepository` isn't in `CLOUD_HUB_OPERATIONS` in #15205, so it won't be reachable through the Hub client. It's also called in both prepare and run (via `resolveCloudModel`), along with `loadCloudModels` and 8 `assertHandoffAccount` calls. Resolving once and carrying a scope token in the snapshot would remove most of the repeated checks.

The missing Hub operation is fixed: `prepareHandoffRepository` is registered in `CLOUD_HUB_OPERATIONS`, validated by the Hub service, and exposed by `CloudHubClient`. The preparation snapshot also captures a `CloudHubScope`, which subsequent operations carry so they cannot silently switch accounts. Socket coverage exercises repository preparation, and account-scope tests cover changes during recovery. This addresses the RPC compatibility issue; it does not remove the repeated model/repository checks.

The current implementation also removes the repeated preparation pass: `resolveCloudModel` runs during preview, and the approved snapshot retains the model, organization, and `CloudHubScope` for launch. `prepareHandoffRepository` is available through the merged Hub client. Account checks still surround asynchronous work so an old approval cannot launch under a different account.

Agree the root alone is not a trust boundary, but there is nothing more trusted to source it from: in this app the webview is what chooses the workspace in the first place (the same connection drives validate_workspace_directory / pick_workspace_directory / open_file_in_editor and starts agent sessions with full file tools). What does matter is that originless local clients are accepted on the transport, so in 8a327a6 these two commands now require the trusted desktop connection (canApproveTools), the same gate agenda task execution uses. The root check stays as a coherence guard for the tree and the comment now says so instead of overclaiming.

Following symlinks here is intentional: bun's node_modules/.bun layout is symlinks, and people link sibling checkouts into a workspace. The reader runs as the user, for the user's own UI (now gated to the trusted desktop connection, see the thread above), so a link resolving outside the root shows the user a file they already own and can open in their editor from the same panel. Rejecting resolved targets would break legitimate trees without closing a real boundary, so I am leaving this as is and documented the intent on assertInsideRoot.
Fixed in 8a327a6: only '..' itself and '../' / '..\\' prefixes are rejected now, with a test for a '..notes' directory.

*high*

`cwd` is granted read-write with no check, and `keep-changes-in-project-extension.ts` seeds `allowedRoots` from `options.cwd` the same way. The safety boundary is therefore whatever directory the session started in: from `~`, all of `~` is writable (I verified this on macOS); from `G:\`, the whole drive. Suggest resolving real paths and failing closed, with a message, when any read-write grant is a volume or filesystem root, the home directory, or an ancestor of it.

*medium*

`hostLoopback: "allow"` is requested on Windows too. MXC's AppContainer fallback rejects a policy with loopback ingress allowed (`appcontainer_runner.rs` in microsoft/mxc), so a Windows host that can only enforce the sandbox through that tier fails every protected command instead of running it restricted. Not requesting ingress unless something needs it (the Linux branch already sends none) lets those hosts work.

*medium*

I saw your reply on the earlier thread that an unknown value should not sandbox. One case still contradicts the comment above this line: `lastReadKeepChangesInProject` starts as `false`, so a process whose very first read of an existing settings file fails (torn write, corrupt file) runs unsandboxed while the user believes the setting is on, and nothing says so. If you'd rather not fail closed, could it at least distinguish "file absent" from "file exists but unreadable" and surface the second case, with a log line or a warning in the tool result, instead of silently staying off?

Fixed. Containment is now a direct-child check against each rule root (or the root itself when it is the single legacy `.clinerules` file), matching what the SDK loader reads. Nested files are skipped and left untouched; test added.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
🟡 **security** (medium)

The `state` parameter is no longer enforced on the auth callback, only used to decide whether to show a confirmation prompt. Combined with the corresponding change in AuthService.ts (`private readonly _authNonce = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("hex")` — a value now generated once per extension lifetime and never rotated), the state check no longer provides any anti-forgery/replay protection: a previously observed or attacker-constructed auth URL remains valid for the whole session, and a forged callback (`<scheme>://saoudrizwan.claude-dev/auth?token=...`) only requires the user to accept one dialog to bind the extension to an attacker-controlled account. The old code rejected mismatched states outright.

**建议**: Keep the convenience path for external sign-ins but restore a real security boundary, e.g. (a) regenerate/rotate the nonce per auth request and accept a state that is a member of a short-lived, bounded set of recent nonces rather than a single lifetime constant, and/or (b) make the confirmation prompt explicitly describe the risk ("this sign-in request could not be verified — continue only if you started it") and default to cancel. At minimum, document why the state check is intentionally downgraded so it is not mistaken for CSRF protection.

Consistent with the existing model, not a new gap: run.abort and session.delete act on any session by id with no ownership check either, and this PR's description calls that out. The owner helper (resolveLiveSessionOwner) lands in #14681; once that is in, gating session.stop, run.abort and session.delete on it is a small follow-up that should happen together rather than one command at a time here.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Addressed. `setRuleDisabledInFrontmatter` now takes the allowed roots for the scope (global Rules directory, or the workspace `.clinerules` directory or single file), resolves the request path through symlinks with `realpath`, requires a regular file inside one of those roots, and only writes the file types the SDK loader reads (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, or the bare `.clinerules` file). Anything else keeps the extension-state toggle only. Tests cover the symlink escape, non-rule files in a rules folder, and relative or missing paths.

For context on severity: the RPC caller is the extension's own webview, the same trust level as the existing skill toggle and rule create/delete handlers, so the practical risk was corrupting a stray non-rule file that happened to live in a rules folder. That is what the containment and extension checks close.
